prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-25. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.42 |
| Retained earnings       | 261,693M |
| Current liabilities     | 2,559,605M |
| Current assets          | 1,067,083M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 303,243M |
| Total liabilities       | 3,107,151M |
| Total assets            | 3,410,394M |
| EBIT / operating income | 12,435M |
| Revenue                 | 49,691M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-25, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits very weak liquidity with a current ratio of 0.42, indicating a significant inability to cover short-term obligations. Furthermore, the debt-to-equity ratio is alarmingly high at 10.24 (3,107,151M / 303,243M), suggesting an over-reliance on debt financing and a highly leveraged capital structure. While EBIT is positive, the substantial debt and poor liquidity present considerable default risk.

DECISION: B-
